Func - Load Functions.vi

Owning Palette: FuncVI Service

The VI can be used to explicitly load FuncVIs to memory.
If CalcExpress needs to call a FuncVI function, it looks for an opened VI reference that refers to the FuncVI. If there is no an opened reference, CalcExpress implicitly opens it; i.e. it makes LabVIEW load the FuncVI. You can reduce time required to perform the first call of a FuncVI if you preliminary load it.
The VI only recognizes function names. It looks for the corresponding FuncVI in search paths defined in Func - FuncVI search paths.vi.

Click the parameters for more information

 

List of func names defines a list of function names to load/unload respective FuncVIs if Array of func names is not wired or is empty. Every line of the list has to contain a function name (not a FuncVI name).
Array of func names defines an array of function names to load/unload respective FuncVIs. If the array is not empty, every element of the array has to contain a function name (not a FuncVI name). If Array of func names is empty (by default), the VI uses List of func names as the source of function names.
test arg num (F) is an optional parameter. If it is TRUE, the VI verifies a number that follows a function name for valid number of parameters on which the function can operate. If a function name is not followed by a number, the VI does not perform the verification. By default, test arg num is FALSE.
error in describes error conditions that occur before this VI runs. This input provides standard error in functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains error code.
source contains additional error information.
loaded functions returns function names whose FuncVIs have been loaded at the current call of the VI. Note that VI only loads FuncVIs that are not loaded yet (more precise, FuncVIs to which CalcExpress doesn't have opened VI Reference).
error message.
error out contains error information. This output provides standard error out functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains error code.
source contains additional error information.
